blocks.content: Article 32 is the very soul of the Constitution and the very heart of it.

items: Articles 15, 16, 19, 29, and 30 are exclusive Fundamental Rights available ONLY to Indian citizens.
The Right to Education was added under Article 21A by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002.
Writs under Article 32 can be issued only by the Supreme Court, while High Courts issue writs under Article 226 with broader scope.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Part III of the Indian Constitution guarantees Fundamental Rights to all citizens from Articles 12 to 35.
The Right to Property was deleted from the list of Fundamental Rights by the 44th Amendment Act, 1978, and made a legal right under Article 300A.
Fundamental Rights are justiciable, meaning individuals can directly move the Supreme Court under Article 32 for their enforcement.
Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended even during a National Emergency declared under Article 352.
